title: Reverse engineering games is like a game itself
author: VirtuePlushies

comments.author: ContemptOfTheZ
comments.body: Except this isn't a game, just a video.

replies.author: VirtuePlushies
replies.body: Correct this is not gameplay just something to keep me engaged while working on it And waiting for usage limit reset, I never thought I would have a reason to reinstall Metal Gear Rising ever again!

comments.author: PhantomZenithOrigin
comments.body: This is just generated video, it has nothing to do with reverse engineering shit.

replies.author: VirtuePlushies
replies.body:
I never claimed it was live gameplay. I literally used the `Media` flair for this post, not `Demo | Project | Workflow`. Coding agents aren't very creative on their own, so I feed them generated visuals and videos as a reference. I am also running the game and doing actual reverse engineering

https://preview.redd.it/5cw19hrsxovh1.png?width=1023&format=png&auto=webp&s=da29b9237339b88c6fd43c27d5b2919283d4c1f2

replies.author: Pokeperson5
replies.body: Ok but what actually is the point of this post. A vague title coupled with an unrelated video?

replies.author: VirtuePlushies
replies.body: Since when does a `Media`\-flaired post need a point? The sub is for exploring generative AI in game dev. I posted a visual concept I'm using in my workflow because I thought it was cool and wanted to share what I'm tinkering with. Last I checked, that doesn't break any rules here. Not everything has to be a deep-dive essay.

replies.author: Pokeperson5
replies.body: Generally all posts have some sort of point, however minor it may be. What I'm mainly confused about here is, what you were actually expecting to gain from this post? More specifically, what were you expecting people to comment about on this?

replies.author: VirtuePlushies
replies.body:
Since when did game dev move past the need for concept art and proof-of-concepts? Just because we're using AI doesn't mean visual references are obsolete. 

In fact, feeding visual targets to coding agents is one of the best ways to get them to build decent UI and mechanics instead of generic boilerplate. That's the conversation I expected to have here.

replies.author: Pokeperson5
replies.body: I'm not sure how you keep misunderstanding my comments? The issue is how vague the post is, that's all, just maybe clarify what it actually is you're sharing next time.

replies.author: VirtuePlushies
replies.body: You're right. Next time, I'll make sure to put **\[THIS IS NOT LIVE GAMEPLAY\]** in giant capital letters, just in case the **MEDIA** flair I specifically chose instead of the **LIVE GAMEPLAY** flair wasn't obvious enough.
